method.type: Structured chapter coverage audit; not exhaustive line-by-line manuscript review and not rendered-artwork approval.
method.scope: 17 canonical numbered chapters. Canonical generated-index source and website welcome alias inspected separately; notes are outside numbered chapter rows. HTML/PDF volume configurations checked for source order; appendices and part dividers are outside this assigned numbered-chapter pass.
method.inputs: Full chapter outlines and all body figure anchors/captions, targeted mechanism prose, relevant margin figures and worked tables/pseudocode. Existing animation catalog treatments were not used as evidence of a need.
method.selection: Figures first: propose only an uncovered spatial/temporal/ownership argument. Existing adequate coverage receives no addition. Existing animation candidates are selective educational proposals, independent of implementation status; maximum three per chapter is a presentation shortlist, not a recommendation to animate every other figure later.
method.deduplication: Checked each proposed gap against body captions and nearby prose/margin art. Notably no redundant new KV overview, continuous-batching, speculative-decoding, paging, or error-feedback body figure.
method.limitations: No source/art edits, no numerical simulation, no student testing, no visual approval. Proposed first/last states must be reconciled with source artwork and technical audit before implementation. Keep-static entries mean no necessary animation identified in this pass, not permanent prohibition.
method.index_note: The PDF config documents generated books/index.qmd as a per-job symlink to books/index-vol2.qmd; the generated index is absent in this worktree. books/vol2/index.qmd is separately linked by the HTML sidebar.

animation_candidates.title: Retryable tasks vs. shared training steps
animation_candidates.reason: The dependency boundary is temporal: some tasks finish independently while a synchronous update waits for every required contribution.
sequence: Complete two map tasks and retain their output records.
Fail and retry only the third map task, then run its dependent reducer.
In the training panel finish two gradients but retain old weights while the third is late.
After the last contribution arrives perform the shared update.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: A straggler on the critical path blocks shared progress; independent task completion does not mean whole-job independence.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional straggler delay with schematic time, preserving reducer dependencies; no fabricated measured speedups.

retired_candidates.title: Tensor Core tiling strategy
retired_candidates.reason: Reuse and partial-sum lifetime cannot be seen as clearly in a single transfer map.
sequence: Read matching A/B K-slices from HBM into shared memory.
Reuse each slice in several MACs while the C partial-sum tile remains in registers.
Replace operand slices and add to the same C tile.
Write completed C once after the final K-slice.
retired_candidates.systems_takeaway: HBM reuse trades on-chip capacity for reduced traffic; partial sums are retained through reduction.
retired_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional tile size with a declared toy byte accounting model and an explicit SRAM/register fit constraint.
retired_candidates.reason_retired: Current dev defers kernel mechanics to the appendix; a single local paragraph no longer warrants a duplicate local animation.

chapters.title: Network Fabrics
chapters.summary: Wire/link, transport, topology, congestion, deployment, virtualization, and diagnostics.
chapters.static_assessment: Existing figures cover GPUDirect copies, link budgets, topology, PFC dependency cycles, and incast. No new diagram is required; animation can selectively expose copies and queue dependencies.

animation_candidates.title: GPUDirect RDMA data path
animation_candidates.reason: The same payload takes different copy paths; host-memory traffic can be accumulated as transfers occur.
sequence: Identify one M-byte tensor in source GPU memory.
Trace GPU-to-host staging and NIC host read, retaining source/copy identity.
Reset to the same payload and trace NIC peer read from GPU memory.
Compare host-memory payload traffic under the caption assumptions.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Removing a host bounce changes copies and resource use, not the physical wire-rate ceiling.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional payload size and count of copies; distinguish host traffic from total interconnect traffic.

animation_candidates.title: A PFC deadlock from a cyclic buffer dependency
animation_candidates.reason: Hold-and-wait and reverse PAUSE direction are inherently causal and easy to confuse in a static cycle.
sequence: Fill downstream queues with packets whose next hop is occupied.
Send PAUSE upstream while retaining packets in each queue.
Close the cyclic dependency; demonstrate that no packet can drain.
Trigger the declared watchdog drop and allow forward progress.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Lossless backpressure can form a dependency deadlock; watchdog recovery sacrifices packets.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional bounded queue capacity/initial placements, with exact queue/packet conservation and no real hardware timing claims.

animation_candidates.title: Two-phase checkpoint staging
animation_candidates.reason: The exposed pause, completed background copy, and committed restore point occur at different moments.
sequence: Pause at a consistent training state and write immutable local shards.
Resume live training while the shards drain to durable storage.
Keep the previous generation as restore point until every shard/checksum is ready.
Publish the new manifest last; only then move the restore pointer.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Resumed execution is not proof that the new checkpoint is durably committed.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional failure injection before/after publication with recoverable generation made explicit.

animation_candidates.title: Pipelined data loading
animation_candidates.reason: Concurrent batch identities and the prefetch queue reveal what overlap hides.
sequence: Run read/prepare/compute sequentially for one batch.
Retain batch identities while read of i+2, prepare of i+1, and compute of i overlap.
Drain the queue when delivery falls behind.
Show exposed GPU input wait rather than continuing useful compute.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Prefetching hides latency only while delivery rate and buffer headroom support it.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional declared stage costs/queue depth; common schematic time axis, no technology-wide utilization claim.

animation_candidates.title: Ring AllReduce data flow
animation_candidates.reason: The two phases change what each rank holds, and partial reductions must not become final sums too early.
sequence: Partition each rank contribution into indexed chunks.
For each ReduceScatter round send one chunk, add received contribution, and retain accumulated provenance.
At the boundary each rank owns one fully reduced chunk.
AllGather finished chunks without summing again until every rank has the full result.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: ReduceScatter plus AllGather produces a replicated sum while paying per-round startup and transfer bytes.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional tiny rank count/chunk values; count sends per rank and distinguish logical ring from physical network.

animation_candidates.title: Communication-computation overlap
animation_candidates.reason: Readiness dependencies determine which network work can actually overlap backward compute.
sequence: Complete the last layer backward and expose its ready gradient.
Launch its AllReduce while the next layer computes backward.
Keep incomplete buckets and dependencies visible.
After the first layer completes show the residual communication tail before optimizer update.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Only transfer intervals supported by concurrent work are hidden; the exposed tail remains on the critical path.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional schematic stage durations or bucket size with explicit readiness/startup assumptions.

animation_candidates.title: Pipeline parallelism schedule
animation_candidates.reason: The figure already provides a correct schedule; animation can preserve each microbatch identity through forward and reverse dependencies.
sequence: Inject one microbatch and retain its saved activations at each stage.
Inject later microbatches into free forward slots.
After forward completion return gradients in the declared GPipe order.
Release each saved activation only after its backward consumer; reveal fill/drain bubbles.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Microbatching fills pipeline slots while saved-state lifetime and dependencies constrain the schedule.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional microbatch count for the same all-forward/all-backward policy; do not silently change to 1F1B.

animation_candidates.title: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) AllToAll routing
animation_candidates.reason: Tokens genuinely change owner twice, and result combination must return to the originating rank.
sequence: Keep token and source-rank IDs.
Route token payloads to selected expert owners.
Compute expert results, leaving unselected experts available for other tokens.
Return results to source ranks and combine using the declared top-1 case.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Sparse arithmetic can create distributed communication and uneven expert queues.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional top-k or routing distribution requires explicit scope change and a load/byte model; no unsupported bisection speedup.

animation_candidates.title: Checkpoint-recovery timeline
animation_candidates.reason: Progress exists in live and durable forms; failure rewinds one while preserving the other.
sequence: Advance live steps beyond a committed checkpoint.
Start a save, withholding durability until completion.
Inject a failure and mark uncommitted work as rework.
Read the last completed checkpoint, restart, then repeat lost steps.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Failure cost includes both rework and restore delay; a save in flight is not the restore point.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional failure instant/checkpoint interval under the chapter cost model, with expected versus realized loss separated.

animation_candidates.title: The distributed deadlock (hold and wait)
animation_candidates.reason: The resource ownership transition explains why a non-gang scheduler can have allocated yet idle GPUs.
sequence: Grant J1 only part of its required gang.
Grant the remaining devices to J2; retain both leases while jobs wait.
Show the resulting no-progress state.
Reset and grant J1 atomically while J2 waits without ownership, then release for J2.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Admission and ownership are different from useful execution; gang allocation prevents this hold-and-wait pattern.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional job sizes and arrival order; no claim that gang scheduling removes every deadlock or fragmentation source.

animation_candidates.title: Operator fusion before and after
animation_candidates.reason: Intermediate tensor writes and rereads are real observable changes, unlike highlighting operators.
sequence: Compute the first unfused intermediate and write it to HBM.
Reread for the next kernel and repeat for the second intermediate.
Replay equal arithmetic in a fused on-chip chain, retaining intermediate identity.
Write only the final activation and compare counted activation transfers.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Fusion removes intermediate traffic subject to kernel feasibility; byte reduction is not proportional latency reduction.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional tensor sizes with byte accounting, keeping weight reads and metadata exclusions visible.

animation_candidates.title: FlashAttention memory hierarchy tiling
animation_candidates.reason: Online rescaling and persistent output/statistics are difficult to infer from a static memory map.
sequence: Load one Q tile and a K/V tile into declared on-chip space.
Compute a local score block without storing the full score matrix in HBM.
On later K/V tiles update running maximum, normalization sum, and rescaled partial output.
After all tiles normalize/write the output and expose workspace/traffic separately.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Exact attention can trade scheduled on-chip reuse and recomputation for avoided quadratic resident intermediates.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional tile capacity/sequence length on a toy case, showing reloads and numerical invariant; not a simple O(S) traffic assertion.

chapters.title: Inference at Scale
chapters.summary: Serving lifecycle, batching, cache capacity and placement, disaggregation, sharding, routing, isolation, scaling, and global deployment.
chapters.static_assessment: Prefill/decode, continuous batching, KV capacity, paging, prefix sharing, disaggregation, and sharding already have figures. Do not duplicate those. Chunked-prefill interference and the shared iteration budget lack a body figure despite a substantial mechanism section and pseudocode.

animation_candidates.title: End-to-end inference pipeline
animation_candidates.reason: Prefill, iterative decode and persistent per-request KV state are foundational temporal mechanisms.
sequence: Admit and tokenize one short prompt with token IDs.
Prefill writes indexed K/V entries for prompt positions at the declared layer/head scope.
Each decode iteration reads retained prior K/V, appends the current position state and emits the next sampled token.
On completion release request-owned cache blocks while model weights remain resident.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Prompt work initializes persistent request state; generation repeatedly reads/extends it, and completion releases it.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional prompt/output lengths and head/precision assumptions; show bytes from declared cache shape, not attention scores or hidden states labeled as KV. Precisely label which consumed token creates each appended entry.

animation_candidates.title: Static vs. continuous batching
animation_candidates.reason: Iteration membership and freed cache capacity change as differently sized requests finish.
sequence: Admit the same four requests under each policy.
Advance a decode iteration while preserving request colors/IDs.
Complete one request and release its KV state.
Static policy leaves its slot unused; continuous policy prefills an admitted waiting request at the next boundary.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Continuous batching recovers slot capacity only when arrivals and memory admission allow replacement.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional arrival/length trace and KV capacity, with slot-iterations separate from elapsed throughput and prefill duration.

animation_candidates.title: KV cache fragmentation and the PagedAttention solution
animation_candidates.reason: Allocation, logical addressing and release are a better lesson than flashing physical slots.
sequence: Replay internal reservation waste with the caption eight-slot example.
Release finished allocations and show fragmented free physical blocks.
Fail contiguous admission for E despite four total free slots.
Allocate E pages to blocks 0,1,4,5, use its block table for reads, then release owned blocks at completion.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: A logical sequence need not occupy contiguous HBM; paging recovers allocatable capacity without compressing KV values.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional block size/request lengths. Prefix sharing can be a later separately introduced scenario with reference counts and copy-on-write; do not silently mix it into the eight-slot example.

animation_candidates.title: Speculative decoding process
animation_candidates.reason: Accepted prefixes, correction and discarded suffixes are changing state with a clear dependency boundary.
sequence: Retain target context while the draft proposes an indexed token run.
Verify the run with the target model.
Accept the valid prefix and stop at the first rejection.
Emit a corrected sample, discard the invalid suffix and restore valid cache state.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Extra draft/verification work only pays when enough output survives; exact sampling requires the specified acceptance/correction rule.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional declared acceptance traces and costs; distinguish an illustrative trace from a distribution guarantee or measured speedup.

reuse_opportunities.title: Chunked prefill: protecting decode without removing prompt work
reuse_opportunities.evidence: The scheduler reserves one token per active decode request, allocates residual iteration budget to prompt slices, advances offsets only after execution, and promotes completed prefills. Lines 2591-2669 describe TBT interference and TTFT trade-off.
reuse_opportunities.existing_coverage: fig-inference-lifecycle (168) is one request; fig-continuous-batching-comparison (1862) replaces finished slots at iteration boundaries but does not split a long prefill across them; fig-disaggregated-serving (4166) instead separates pools. The roofline margin figure explains intensity, not scheduling.
reuse_opportunities.proposal: Same request arrivals in two timelines: a long monolithic prefill delays existing streams; chunked prefill interleaves bounded prompt chunks with decode iterations. Under the second timeline show one hybrid token tray with decode tokens reserved first, residual prompt allocation, persistent prompt offset and KV progress. Mark the long prompt first-token boundary and existing stream gaps. Reuse the same arrival/timing assumptions as the source timeline, or explicitly declare and recompute any changed workload.
reuse_opportunities.why_static: Print must show both the interrupted streams and the long prompt completion boundary; pseudocode alone obscures whose latency is exchanged. Use schematic iteration slots rather than imply equal token budgets mean equal duration.
reuse_opportunities.animation_value: High: reader commits one iteration at a time, sees decode tokens emitted, prompt offset/KV built, and completed prefill promoted. An optional lab varies chunk budget under a stated timing model and reports both TTFT and TBT, not guaranteed SLO satisfaction.

animation_candidates.title: TinyTL adaptation paths

sequence: Run forward through frozen backbone and trainable bias/lite modules.

Propagate gradients through frozen blocks to trainable modules.

animation_candidates.title: Point-in-time correctness
animation_candidates.reason: The reader can observe which events are available at the prediction moment while later data remain excluded.
sequence: Append four click events up to noon.
Freeze the noon example and its available feature value at 4.
Append six later events while preserving the noon cutoff.
Compare the legal historical join with an illegal midnight total of 10.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: A valid database value can still be unavailable for the prediction moment; feature construction must preserve historical availability.

animation_candidates.title: Shadow and canary deployment
animation_candidates.reason: Requests are copied in shadowing but partitioned in canarying, and only one path may reply to the user.
sequence: Mirror a request to production and shadow candidate; retain both copy IDs.
Return only production output and send candidate output to comparison.
Switch the declared example to a canary traffic split and route distinct requests to each model.
Hold or roll back the rollout when a declared gate fails.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Evaluation traffic can double compute while user exposure remains zero; canarying instead exposes a controlled user slice.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional canary fraction and capacity budget with synthetic pass/fail outcomes; no automated release claim from insufficient evidence.

needs.title: A drift alert traced to the first changed pipeline tensor
needs.evidence: The worked example has identical golden raw inputs across two versions, a constant-factor change in preprocessed features after a dependency update, and changed model decisions despite healthy uptime.

needs.proposal: Paired old/current pipelines with the same golden input IDs: raw inputs match -> preprocessing values diverge -> predictions differ. needs.why_static: The static side-by-side comparison exposes the diagnostic evidence and prevents the drift alarm from being read as proof of environmental change.
needs.animation_value: Medium: reveal matched stage results until the first divergence and ask the reader which artifact to investigate; actual tensor values change, rather than blue boxes walking over a pipeline. Treat evidence as a toy diagnosis, not a universal classifier of root cause.
